# CG-RES-020: Response media type removed

A response no longer offers a media type.

**Why it matters:** Consumers request media types; removal narrows accepted negotiation (area: request).

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Area | [Responses](./#res) |
| Direction | response |
| Detects | `mediaType.removed` |
| Severity | breaking: high · potentially breaking: medium · undetermined: medium |
| Classification can be overridden | no (the rule only fires when the change is breaking by definition) |

## Message

> Response media type {mediaType} was removed from {where}.
>
> Consumers that request {mediaType} via Accept may receive 406 or a different format.
>
> **Fix:** Keep offering {mediaType}, or release as a new major version.

## Examples

Each example is an executed test case of the rule (`packages/engine/test/compat/fixtures.ts`).

### Fires: application/xml removed from 200

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok, content: {application/json: {}, application/xml: {}}}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok, content: {application/json: {}}}}
```

**Result:** Breaking, high. Response media type application/xml was removed from GET /x: response 200 (application/xml).

### Does not fire: normalization-only difference

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok, content: {Application/JSON: {}}}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok, content: {application/json: {}}}}
```

**Result:** no finding from this rule.

## Limitations

- Server negotiation fallbacks are unknown.

## Silence or tune it

```yaml
rules:
  ignore:
    - rule: CG-RES-020
      operation: "GET /example"   # optional: narrow it down
      reason: "Explain why this is acceptable"
      expires: 2027-01-01         # optional
  overrides:
    CG-RES-020: { severity: low }
```
